August 15, 2026 – On Friday, the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for August was released.  
  
Note: August 2024 Consumer Sentiment under President Biden was 67.9  
  
The following is from Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu: [...] Consumer sentiment fell about 8% this August, ending two consecutive months of improvement. While views of personal finances saw only minor declines, expected business conditions sank 11% for the short run and 17% for the long run. Decreases in sentiment were seen across the political spectrum, with Republicans exhibiting the strongest month-to-month decline in August. ## Key Takeaways

1.   The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index preliminary reading fell to 51 in August, a 7.6% decrease from July.

2.   The Current Economic Conditions Index fell 16.0% to 51.8, while the Consumer Expectations Index fell 9.5% to 50.6.
3.   Year-ahead inflation expectations increased from 4.3% from 4.2% in July.
